Some disturbing news out of Texas, but it’s apparently not limited to the Lone Star State. It seems that the DEA has been investigating so called “pill mills” to crack down on doctors getting a little too enthusiastic with their prescription pads. That’s a worthy issue to look into if it’s happening in large numbers but it comes with a built in problem. If these doctors are writing prescriptions, then by definition they must be writing them for patients. And if the DEA wants a peek at those patients’ confidential medical records they need to get a warrant.

Or do they? (Fox News)

Drug Enforcement Administration agents have been accessing personal medical files without a warrant, generating a backlash from doctors and privacy advocates who say the practice is intrusive and unconstitutional — and have taken the agency to court.

“It’s just not right,” Texas attorney Terri Moore said.

The controversial record searches are part of the government’s effort to crack down on illegal “pill mills” and prescription drug abuse. But they’ve set up a clash over privacy rights, and a legal battle is now playing out in the 5th and 9th Circuit appeals courts. Lower courts have issued conflicting rulings to date, with one backing the DEA and another demanding the agency get warrants if it wants to look at patient records.

I work in a pharmacy. They are not seizing patient records without a warrant. What happens is the DEA has a central data base that collects information on when someone fills a control substance. This operates in most states; however, some states ban it. This is essential information to keep people from going to different doctors and filling different prescriptions for the same medication otherwise there would be no way to know if someone was filling different prescriptions for say oxycodone from different pharmacies.

Only certain people have access to this information. What it shows is only controlled substances, it shows who wrote it and, how much, how long it should last, and where you got it from.

Hi guys,

I haven't been pushing many updates lately, this is mainly due to not having as many missing features as before. Currently the main missing feature is posting, however, that's not possible because:

  • Lack of an API
  • Voat.co requires a captcha when submitting via the website which is not possible to replicate. I don't know why it sometimes ask for a captcha and sometimes not. If I add that feature now it will fail when there is a captcha required and people won't be happy about that specially that they can't see why it would fail.

So, since there aren't many outstanding missing features now, I think I should focus on the UI.

I have decided to completely rewrite the UI from scratch and I'm currently in the process of doing so. The reason I want to do that is because the current UI is written in a cross-platform way which is really limiting in terms of taking advantage of native Android UI stuff like floating buttons, animated cards and future cool UI stuff that Google keeps adding. I want the app to be ready for the future to take advantage of any new native Android UI idea that I want to implement. Just to give an example, I'm currently unable to do the swipe between pages navigation animation even though it would be pretty simple if I were using the native Android SDK directly.

It might take some time, but I think it's for the best really, I'll still try to push some cool updates while doing the rewrite. I have some ideas in mind that I want to add before publishing the new rewritten Boat.

Hope you guys can wait a bit with me, I think it will be worth the effort :)
